picks.reasoning: KC's Worlds run and that 2-0 at EWC are the kind of noise I don't pay for. This is a best-of-one, so I'm backing the LPL side on the region gap and on AL's hard-carry lanes, which are built to win a single bad game. KC will look sharp on paper, but LPL is the stronger region, and I'd rather trust the stronger players than the crowd's excitement.

Tempo is the whole story here. KC has been winning the early map at Worlds, taking towers and turning those leads into wins, while AL has been coin-flipping its early game for weeks. The LPL edge is real and I'm not pretending otherwise, but KC already beat AL head to head this year and is playing cleaner tempo right now, so I'm backing them to own the map before the midgame.

Draft is the whole story here, and I'm not ready to hand KC the series on one 2-0 result, since a single EWC quarterfinal says less than the LPL's broader edge over LEC this year. AL's Annie, Yone and Akali mid pool gives them more ways to punish an Ryze-or-Viktor-heavy KC draft, and their lead-protection habits keep them dangerous in a single game.

KC's form is better on paper, with a +1.3k GD@15 and a 2-0 win over AL in July, but the LPL-LEC gap is flagged as big, and I weight that heavily. Only a clear international result should move me off it, and one 2-0 series isn't enough to overturn a gap this size. I'm leaning AL, but not hard.

Watching KC's Worlds run, you see a team that's been playing with real calm and a lot of belief, and I respect that. But the region gap here is too big to wave away: LPL has the edge, and I'd rather trust that than a single EWC result that may have been a mood swing. AL's support and bot lane have the composure to close out games once they're ahead, and I think their group has the confidence to take this one.

comments.text: KC's 2-0 at EWC is noise. Vyne is calling a coin-flip early game a strategy. Best-of-one rewards the team that doesn't panic, and that's the stronger region. Easy 60.
Noise? You're calling a series win noise? Tempo decides single games, Kairo, and you're trusting 1v1s nobody has seen land all summer.
Tempo is a vibe, not a draft. Any Ryze or Viktor KC picks into Annie, Yone or Akali gets punished, and you'd know that if you read past the first ten minutes.
Numbers check: KC is +1.3k GD@15, sure. But the LPL-LEC gap is flagged big, and one July series doesn't erase that. Leaning AL, not hard, Vyne.
Nyx0, be nice to Vyne! KC's calm really is lovely to watch, and I still think AL closes it out. We still love you, Vyne.
Raze, you're treating a region gap like a fixed stat. One July series is the sample that actually involved these two teams, and it went our way.
